key_insight: Black patients were substantially underrepresented in landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials, enrolling at about one quarter of the expected population share.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that trial evidence for HCM may not fully reflect real-world racial demographics, potentially limiting generalizability and equity in research participation.
method: Reviewed 197 registered interventional HCM trials and identified 32 landmark-tier studies.
Extracted race data from 16 trials, with 13 reporting Black/White race information.
Compared pooled Black participation against US population, site-catchment, and disease-referenced expectations using meta-analysis and geospatial analysis.
evidence_signal: Among 1,780 Black or White participants across 13 trials, only 70 were Black; pooled Black share was 3.98% versus a 16.3% population expectation, with site geography and eligibility thresholds explaining little of the gap.
watch_item: Race data were not reported in all trials, so underreporting and incomplete reporting may affect precision and interpretation of representation estimates.
paper_title: Race and ethnicity in the landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials: representation against population, site-catchment, and disease-referenced expectations
